free_tier.stated: Free plan, EUR 0: 100 requests a day, up to 10 articles a request, articles 12 hours late, 30 days of history.
free_tier.notes: The counter resets at 00:00 UTC and unused requests do not carry over. Article content is truncated to a short excerpt on the Free plan, and pagination stops at 1,000 articles a query. CORS allows only localhost. The next plan up is Essential at EUR 49.99 a month for 1,000 requests a day. A free education plan built on Essential (1,000 requests a day, 25 articles a request, history back to 2020, full content) is granted after a manual review to students, researchers and teaching staff at a recognised institution.

per_object_cap.stated: 10 articles a request on the Free plan; content truncated to a short excerpt
per_object_cap.notes: unverified: behind a sign-up. The first-party pages say only 'a short excerpt' for the Free plan content and give no length. Sample responses show an excerpt of 250 characters followed by '... [N chars]' (the documentation's JSON sample and a third-party sample of ten articles), and a third-party benchmark on a Free key reported a median visible content length of 265 characters over 80 values.

retention.stated: search reaches the last 30 days, and articles appear after a 12-hour delay

interface_detail: REST over HTTPS: GET /api/v4/search and /api/v4/top-headlines, with the key in the apikey parameter
tooling: any HTTP client; official Python, JavaScript and PHP packages
chaining: Headline and article-metadata search with the article URL in each result; the full page is fetched separately by a crawler.

limits.value: 100 requests a day on the Free plan, reset at 00:00 UTC; over it the API answers 403
1 request a second on the Free plan; over it the API answers 429
10 articles a request on the Free plan; pagination stops at 1,000 articles a query

binding_note: 100 requests a day is the first ceiling; at 10 articles a request that is at most 1,000 articles a day.

identity_cost.detail: The sign-up form asks for an email and a password, or Google sign-in, and the email is verified; the Free plan never asks for payment details. A trial of a paid plan asks for a payment method.

reliability_note: Over the daily quota the API answers 403 until 00:00 UTC, and over 1 request a second it answers 429; the 99.95% uptime commitment covers only the Business and Enterprise plans.
confidence_note: unverified: behind a sign-up. The 101st request of a day answering 403, a second request inside one second answering 429 and the Free plan content excerpt length need a free key and were not measured: the 403 and the 429 are documented, and no first-party page states the excerpt length. Quota, delay, history window, rate and sign-up fields are read from first-party pages (pricing, FAQ, error handling); a call with no key answered HTTP 400 'You did not provide an API key.', which the error handling page documents for a missing key. A call with a free key would move this to measured.
